ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low-intensity (black) pixels occupy approximately 85-90% of the fluke surface area, with high-intensity (white) pixels concentrated at the distal left tip and scattered punctate regions.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white blob at the far left distal tip; secondary white patch on the lower right distal margin; multiple discrete circular white clusters (mottling) distributed across the central and right lobe regions on a primary black background.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 42 degrees; vertical depth from the surrounding trailing edge peaks is roughly 12% of the total vertical frame height of the fluke.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Left lobe exhibits 4-5 distinct irregular peaks of varying amplitude; right lobe displays a significant large concave pixel-gap (tissue loss) approximately two-thirds from the notch, followed by smaller, irregular serrations toward the right tip.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Lobes exhibit a general convex sweep outward from the notch, with an upward vertical trajectory becoming more pronounced toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Spatial detection of at least 12 distinct circular white ring-like clusters ranging from 4-10 pixels in diameter, primarily located in the central-left and mid-right regions of the ventral surface.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Detection of multiple horizontal and diagonal faint light-grey linear streaks (rake marks) crossing the black pigment on the inner right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Major traumatic indentation/missing tissue on the trailing edge of the right lobe; dense white calcareous clusters (barnacles) localized at the extreme left margin; significant scarring at the left tip.
other_distinctive_markers: The large missing segment on the upper right trailing edge serves as the primary unique morphological identifier.
